clue.text: Half bottle man? On the contrary

parts.note: demi- is the prefix meaning half, as in demigod
John is a common man's name, standing for any man

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man is a half-bottle sort, then corrects himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' tells you to swap the order of the reading: not a half-bottle man but a half-man bottle, i.e. DEMI (half) + JOHN (man) making a bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A demijohn is a large narrow-necked glass or stoneware bottle, often wicker-covered, used for wine or home brewing.

clue.text: Remove the cad-so unruly:

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the cad are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bounder behaves so badly that he must be thrown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach is to separate or take something off.

clue.text: Horace's peaky parents of unlikely offspring

definitions.text: Horace's peaky parents of unlikely offspring

parts.words: Horace's peaky parents of unlikely offspring
parts.note: the Roman poet wrote that peaks will labour and give birth to a ridiculous mouse; peaky means having peaks, not looking ill

explanation.surface: A man named Horace has sickly-looking parents with surprising children.
explanation.walkthrough: Horace's 'Ars Poetica' has 'parturiunt montes, nascetur ridiculus mus': the mountains are in labour, and a silly mouse is born. 'Peaky' suggests pale and ill.
explanation.definitionFit: In Horace's proverb, great peaks labour and bring forth only a mouse.

clue.text: Maybe Bob and Jim love to spar

indicators.note: maybe signals that the letters are only one possible arrangement, to be rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, the letter O

explanation.surface: Two friends who enjoy boxing practice together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spar' looks like boxing; it is a ship's pole. Rearranging BOB, JIM and O gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A jib boom is a spar run out from the bowsprit of a sailing ship to carry a jib.

clue.text: One is encouraged to take it

definitions.text: One is encouraged to take it

parts.words: One is encouraged to take it
parts.note: the idiom for gaining courage uses the organ that stands for courage, which one is urged to take

explanation.surface: A general remark that someone is urged to accept something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take heart' means be encouraged, so one who is encouraged takes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The organ traditionally seen as the seat of courage, as in the idiom urging someone not to lose hope.

clue.text: Fasten broken plates with wire?

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of plates are smashed and put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: Advice on mending crockery by clamping the shards with wire.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a staple is a piece of bent wire used to fasten things, and old china menders really did rivet broken plates with wire staples.
explanation.definitionFit: To staple is to fix papers or objects together with a U-shaped piece of wire driven through them.

clue.text: Skating around till money comes in

indicators.note: around suggests the letters of skating are spun about into a new order

explanation.surface: A rink makes money from people skating round it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like 'until' but is the cash register.
explanation.definitionFit: The cash a shop or business receives, collected in the register.

clue.text: Namely this man blows 15

parts.note: the name of this man is also criminal slang for a strongbox, and adding man to it gives the safe-blower's cant name

explanation.surface: A certain man, who is named, blows up the strongboxes.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'peter' is underworld slang for a safe (15 across), and a peterman is a safe-blower, so the man's name plus 'man' does the blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name that is also old thieves' slang for a safe, whose blower is a peterman.

clue.text: Deserted by the repetitious nymph

parts.note: the Greek nymph doomed to repeat others' last words has left, so the place has no repeated sound

explanation.surface: Someone abandoned by a nymph who keeps saying the same things.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the nymph Echo could only repeat what others said; to be without her is to lack reverberation.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any reverberating repetition of sound, as in a dead acoustic space.

clue.text: It yielded the prize to a corner-boy

definitions.text: It yielded the prize to a corner-boy

parts.words: It yielded the prize to a corner-boy
parts.note: the nursery-rhyme boy sat in a corner and pulled a plum from his pie, so the fruit came from this tree

explanation.surface: A street-corner lad wins a prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Jack Horner 'sat in a corner' and 'pulled out a plum'; 'corner-boy' is also a term for a street loafer.
explanation.definitionFit: The fruit tree that bears the sweet stone fruit Jack Horner pulled from his pie.

clue.text: Very little work on hand for the artist

definitions.text: Very little work on hand for the artist

parts.words: Very little work on hand for the artist
parts.note: reads like a painter with few commissions, but means a tiny drawing, small enough to fit on the nail of a digit

explanation.surface: A painter has few commissions at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On hand' looks like 'available', but literally points to a part of the hand, the size of a quick little drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough small drawing or brief outline description is named after the size of a digit's nail.

clue.text: Vessel rigged for a guitarist's wedding-trip ?

definitions.text: Vessel rigged for a guitarist's wedding-trip ?

parts.words: Vessel rigged for a guitarist's wedding-trip ?
parts.note: Edward Lear's owl sang to a small guitar and sailed off to marry its pussy in a pea-green craft, so a feline plus a sailing vessel

explanation.surface: A musician's honeymoon is spent on a specially fitted-out yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lear's 'The Owl and the Pussy-cat' the owl, the guitarist, went to sea with the cat in a boat and they were married; a catboat is also a real single-masted sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A catboat is a small sailing vessel with a single mast stepped far forward carrying one sail.

clue.text: Dog without a tree

parts.note: the tree is a family tree, so this is a hound lacking any recorded pedigree, not one with nowhere to cock its leg

explanation.surface: A dog finds there is no tree in sight.
explanation.definitionFit: A cross-bred dog of no known breed has no pedigree, the family tree breeders record.

clue.text: Circle line put off about one in the morning

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the word for put off is placed around the other pieces

parts.note: to deter someone is to put them off doing something
the Roman numeral for one is I
a.m. stands for ante meridiem, in the morning

explanation.surface: A London Underground Circle line service is cancelled at around one in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Circle line' is London's Underground loop line, but here it means a straight line across a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is a straight line passing through the centre of a circle from one side to the other.

clue.text: Mark other fish when trying for trout

parts.note: a tick is a mark made on paper
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: An angler marks down the other fish caught while after trout.
explanation.walkthrough: Trout tickling is catching trout by stroking their bellies by hand until they can be flipped out of the water.
explanation.definitionFit: Catching trout by hand, gently stroking beneath the fish before grabbing it.

clue.text: Some have " clunk-click " combinations at opening time

definitions.text: Some have " clunk-click " combinations at opening time

parts.words: Some have " clunk-click " combinations at opening time
parts.note: the combinations are number codes turned with a clunk and a click when strongboxes are opened, not seatbelt routines

explanation.surface: Echoes the British road-safety slogan 'Clunk click every trip' about fastening seatbelts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clunk click every trip' was a 1970s British seatbelt campaign, which steers you toward cars; the combinations are really lock codes on strongboxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong lockable cabinets for valuables often open by dialling a numerical combination.

clue.text: Prepared for war, thanks to previous warning

explanation.surface: Someone got ready for battle because they were told in advance.
explanation.definitionFit: Armed beforehand, ready to fight; and the proverb 'forewarned is forearmed' says advance notice gives that readiness.

clue.text: Weakened by a partner's admission ?

explanation.surface: Someone's partner confesses to something damaging.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PAIRED, it is what someone with a partner would admit.
explanation.definitionFit: Damaged or diminished in strength; and split up it is a coupled person's statement of being matched.

clue.text: Enquire in writing for special feature films

indicators.note: in tells you one piece goes inside the other, the enquiring inside the writing

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a piece of writing
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: Someone writes in to ask about special-feature movies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature films' suggests cinema; here a film is a thin covering and the feature is the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Face coverings, including the thin cosmetic layers spread over the face, cover one's features.

clue.text: Gleam of a medal in a 21 of sorts

indicators.note: in places the medal inside the word for a sort of thrower

parts.note: 21 down is a thrower, and one who shies is a sort of thrower
MM is the Military Medal

explanation.surface: The shine of a medal on a potter.
explanation.walkthrough: To shy is to throw (as at a coconut shy), so a shier is a kind of thrower (21 down).
explanation.definitionFit: A shimmer is a soft, wavering gleam of light.

clue.text: Being made from malt or rye

explanation.surface: Something is brewed or distilled from grain.
explanation.definitionFit: A living being is a creation of nature; 'the creature' is an old Irish and Scottish name for whisky, distilled from malt or rye.

clue.text: Potter giving a party?

explanation.surface: A pottery maker hosting a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: A potter throws pots on the wheel, and one who throws a party gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: A craftsman who shapes clay on a wheel; and someone who hosts a party throws it.

clue.text: Lent money paid out on this date

definitions.text: Lent money paid out on this date

parts.words: Lent money paid out on this date
parts.note: Lent is the season before Easter, not the past of lend: special coins are handed out by the monarch on the day before Good Friday

explanation.surface: A loan was repaid on a particular day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lent money' looks like a loan; it is Lent, the church season, when the sovereign distributes Maundy money on the Thursday before Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thursday before Easter, when the British monarch gives specially minted silver coins to elderly people.

clue.text: Where workers contribute to their rise

definitions.text: Where workers contribute to their rise

parts.words: Where workers contribute to their rise
parts.note: workers are worker insects, and the rise is the mound of earth they build up, not a pay increase

explanation.surface: A workplace where staff help earn their own pay increase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' and 'rise' suggest a pay deal; the workers are worker ants and the rise is a heap of soil.
explanation.definitionFit: A mound of earth and debris built by colonies of insects that toil for the nest.

clue.text: Loaded like the bo'sun of the Nancy Bell?

definitions.text: like the bo'sun of the Nancy Bell?

explanation.surface: A sailor in a Gilbert ballad who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: W. S. Gilbert's 'Yarn of the Nancy Bell' lists among its crew 'the bo'sun tight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Drunk, the slang sense of loaded; Gilbert's ballad names the bo'sun as drunk in its catalogue of crew.

clue.text: A major in 25 dn's army, rather than in 26

definitions.text: A major in 25 dn's army, rather than in 26

parts.words: A major in 25 dn's army, rather than in 26
parts.note: the army is the Salvation Army founded by the man at 25 down, and the major is the heroine of a Shaw play, an officer there rather than in a female military unit

explanation.surface: An officer serves in one man's army instead of a women's regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw's play 'Major Barbara' has a heroine who is a major in the Salvation Army, founded by General William Booth (25 down); 26 is the regiment of women.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw's title character is a Salvation Army officer holding the rank of major.

clue.text: William was generally superior to 25 ac

definitions.text: William was generally superior to 25 ac

parts.words: William was generally superior to 25 ac
parts.note: generally means holding the rank of General: the founder of the Salvation Army outranked the Shaw heroine who was a major in it

explanation.surface: A man named William was usually better than someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generally' seems to mean 'usually'; it means as a General. General William Booth founded the Salvation Army, so he outranked Major Barbara.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Methodist preacher who founded the Salvation Army and took the title General.

clue.text: Uniformly monstrous, according to Knox

parts.note: John Knox's tract denounced the monstrous rule of female monarchs, and uniformly hints at a military unit in uniform

explanation.surface: A reformer judges something consistently hideous.
explanation.walkthrough: John Knox, the Scottish Protestant reformer, wrote 'The First Blast of the Trumpet Against the Monstrous Regiment of Women' (1558); 'regiment' there meant rule, but 'Uniformly' plays on soldiers in uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: Knox's famous phrase about rule by queens, punned as a uniformed army unit of females.

clue.text: Point a way for the old fellow

parts.note: a point is a dot
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: Someone shows an old man which way to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A doddering old man, feeble in mind through age.

clue.text: See 22
